interpretation: Structural validity and traceability do not establish completeness or learner readiness. Higher-level sources, alternate paths, and other source outcomes are inspection signals, not automatic defects. Do not delete edges or split decks without evaluating their contracts.

exclusions.subject: mathematics
exclusions.rationale: Forcing, large cardinals and derived or higher geometry are specialist extensions. Set foundations remain in mathematics/set-theory:axiomatic-sets, ordinal-recursion, cardinal-choice; classical geometry remains in mathematics/algebraic-geometry:variety-ideal-correspondence, projective-geometry, local-geometric-structure.

exclusions.subject: computer-science
exclusions.domain: Specialist hardware fabrication and emerging architectures
exclusions.rationale: Hardware fabrication qualifications and exhaustive emerging architecture catalogs are not curricular destinations; architecture foundations remain in computer-science/computer-organization:digital-logic, instruction-execution, memory-hierarchy.

exclusions.subject: chemistry
exclusions.rationale: Plant-scale chemical engineering, licensed hazardous operations and clinical prescribing are separate professional destinations, not assumed outcomes.

exclusions.subject: physics
exclusions.rationale: Quantum-gravity proposals and exhaustive beyond-Standard-Model catalogs are specialist frontiers. Established bases remain in physics/general-relativity:einstein-equations and physics/quantum-field-theory:field-quantization, perturbative-field-methods, renormalization-foundations.

exclusions.subject: biology
exclusions.rationale: Medical, veterinary and regulated clinical diagnostic qualifications are separate professional programs. Disease mechanisms remain included in biology/animal-physiology:physiological-failure, biology/immunology:immune-regulation-pathology, biology/signaling-and-cancer:cancer-evolution and biology/infection-biology:pathogenesis-mechanisms.

includes: Comparative animal tissues/organs, circulation/respiration, digestion/excretion, endocrine/reproductive regulation and homeostatic failure.

outcomes.description: Use pressure-flow, diffusion and gas-binding models taught locally to explain circulation and respiration.
Explain endocrine feedback and reproductive cycles and predict outcomes of defined hormonal perturbations.
Interpret physiological measurements to distinguish compensatory feedback from organ-system failure without making clinical diagnoses.
Apply mass-balance and gradient reasoning to digestion, nutrient absorption, renal clearance and osmoregulation.
Identify major tissues and organs and relate comparative anatomy to physiological function.

practice: Analyze comparative anatomy and physiological time-series cases using explicitly taught flow, clearance and feedback calculations.

includes: Ethograms and behavioral sampling, proximate/ultimate explanations, foraging/mating models, learning and social behavior.

outcomes.description: Evaluate foraging, mating and kin-selection hypotheses using explicitly taught cost-benefit and inclusive-fitness models.
Construct ethograms and unbiased behavioral sampling protocols with observer-agreement checks.
Distinguish learning, social transmission and communication mechanisms through controlled behavioral comparisons.

practice: Code approved or archived behavioral observations and evaluate competing mechanistic and adaptive hypotheses.

includes: Protein, nucleic-acid, lipid and carbohydrate structure; folding, binding equilibria and algebraic enzyme kinetics.

outcomes.description: Calculate fractional occupancy and dissociation constants and distinguish affinity, cooperativity and binding specificity.
Relate biomolecular sequence, stereochemistry and noncovalent interactions to folding, assembly and function.
Interpret catalytic mechanisms and Michaelis-Menten/inhibition curves using explicitly stated steady-state assumptions.

practice: Interpret binding and enzyme datasets with algebraic models and propose molecular explanations for altered activity.

includes: Cellular life, organization and energy, heredity, variation, evolution and biological evidence.

outcomes.description: Distinguish evolutionary explanations from purposeful narratives and evaluate basic observational and experimental evidence.
Explain how reproduction transmits information while mutation and recombination generate variation.
Compare cellular organization and levels of biological organization using explicitly introduced matter and energy concepts.

practice: Interpret organism and cell observations and construct evidence-based explanations separating mechanism from evolutionary history.

includes: Biomolecular free-energy landscapes, polymer elasticity, membrane curvature/transport and single-molecule kinetic inference.

outcomes.description: Derive folding, binding and polymer-force predictions from partition functions and energy-landscape models.
Apply locally developed membrane curvature-energy and transport models to deformation and permeability measurements.
Infer state kinetics from single-molecule dwell times and force measurements with missed-event and heterogeneity checks.

practice: Derive and compare physical models for folding, membrane or single-molecule datasets with parameter and resolution limits explicit.

includes: Membranes and transport, organelles and trafficking, cytoskeleton, cell cycle and microscopy-image interpretation.

outcomes.description: Explain cell-cycle transitions and checkpoints and interpret perturbations of division control.
Relate cytoskeletal polymers and motors to cell shape, movement and image-based organization.
Explain membrane structure and predict passive, facilitated and active transport from molecular and gradient conditions.
Trace protein and membrane trafficking and infer organelle defects from localization evidence.

practice: Annotate cell images and predict localization, transport and division phenotypes from defined molecular perturbations.

includes: Biodiversity threats, fragmentation, genetic diversity, reserve/restoration planning and adaptive management under uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Design adaptive monitoring and intervention comparisons that separate management effects from background change.
Assess biodiversity loss and distinguish habitat, exploitation, invasive-species and climate mechanisms using evidence.
Compare reserve, connectivity and restoration alternatives using transparent biological criteria and uncertainty.

practice: Develop a conservation decision dossier with competing interventions, monitoring design and explicit ecological tradeoffs.

includes: Fate specification, morphogens, gene-regulatory patterning, morphogenesis, regeneration and lineage/perturbation experiments.

outcomes.description: Explain competence, induction and positional information and infer fate-control networks from perturbations.
Design and interpret lineage-tracing, transplantation and temporal perturbation experiments with appropriate controls.
Relate adhesion, polarity and cell mechanics to morphogenesis, organogenesis and regeneration.

practice: Reconstruct a developmental mechanism from lineage and perturbation data and propose discriminating follow-up experiments.

includes: Quadrat/transect/capture-recapture sampling, population growth, species interactions, communities and ecosystem material/energy budgets.

outcomes.description: Estimate abundance and diversity using field sampling designs and identify detectability and spatial-sampling bias.
Construct ecosystem energy and nutrient budgets and explain productivity, decomposition and disturbance responses.
Interpret discrete population growth and species-interaction evidence across terrestrial and aquatic communities.

practice: Analyze a field survey with detectability and uncertainty checks and construct a community or ecosystem budget.

includes: Incidence/prevalence and risk, epidemiological designs, bias, censoring, outbreak curves and compartmental transmission models.

outcomes.description: Estimate rates, risks and adjusted associations and diagnose selection, measurement and confounding bias.
Construct Kaplan-Meier estimates and outbreak summaries with censoring, denominators and ascertainment assumptions checked.
Derive and time-step elementary SIR models and calculate reproduction thresholds and intervention sensitivities.

practice: Analyze an anonymized cohort and outbreak dataset and compare observed patterns with a documented compartment model.

includes: Selection, drift, mutation and migration; adaptation; speciation; phylogenetic evidence and comparative historical inference.

outcomes.description: Calculate elementary allele-frequency changes and distinguish selection, drift, migration and mutation explanations.
Construct small character-based trees and distinguish homology, convergence and ancestral-state uncertainty.
Evaluate reproductive-isolation and diversification hypotheses using genetic, ecological and fossil evidence.

practice: Compare evolutionary explanations for supplied population and fossil cases and construct alternative character trees.

includes: Evolution of developmental networks, regulatory change, heterochrony, homology and comparative perturbation design.

outcomes.description: Infer developmental evolutionary changes while separating homology, convergence, regulatory divergence and timing shifts.
Design comparative perturbation studies that distinguish causal developmental changes from phylogenetic and assay confounding.

practice: Prepare a comparative developmental research proposal with alternative evolutionary histories, perturbation logic and falsifiable predictions.

includes: Biological controls, pipetting and asepsis, extraction/PCR/electrophoresis, microscopy, assay normalization and reproducible records.

outcomes.description: Acquire or analyze calibrated microscopy images with resolution, segmentation and sampling limitations documented.
Design biological experiments with controls, replication, blinding and contamination-aware sample handling.
Plan and perform approved extraction, amplification and separation assays and diagnose control failures.
Maintain sample provenance and reproducible spreadsheet analyses with normalization and exclusion decisions justified.

practice: Complete an approved molecular or imaging investigation with controls, raw records, quantitative analysis and a failure audit.

includes: Mendelian and non-Mendelian inheritance, pedigrees, linkage/recombination and elementary quantitative traits.

outcomes.description: Calculate cross and pedigree probabilities and discriminate Mendelian, sex-linked, cytoplasmic and penetrance models.
Infer gene order and map distances from recombination and test linkage predictions.
Distinguish genetic, environmental and interaction contributions to quantitative traits and interpret elementary heritability estimates.

practice: Analyze crosses and pedigrees and compare alternative inheritance models with probability calculations.

includes: Sequence alignment and assembly, read quality, variant inference, gene expression, enrichment and reproducible genomic workflows.

outcomes.description: Build reproducible genomic workflows with reference versions, provenance, validation and privacy-aware data handling.
Analyze normalized expression and enrichment data with experimental-unit, batch and multiplicity controls.
Analyze read quality and infer variants using locally taught read-error likelihoods and mapping-bias checks.
Implement sequence alignment and elementary overlap/de Bruijn assembly and explain scoring and ambiguity.

practice: Implement a sequence method and complete an archived genomic analysis with controls, provenance and independent validation.

includes: Innate sensing, antigen presentation, lymphocyte diversity/selection, immune memory, tolerance and immune assays.

outcomes.description: Trace antigen presentation, receptor diversification and lymphocyte activation through adaptive and memory responses.
Interpret immunoassay and flow-cytometry readouts using locally taught gating, controls and specificity checks.
Explain tolerance, hypersensitivity, autoimmunity and immune deficiency using cellular mechanisms.
Explain innate sensing, inflammation and complement and predict their tissue-level consequences.

practice: Analyze immune-response and assay datasets, including false-positive, gating and tolerance-failure cases.

includes: Bacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic pathogenesis, tissue damage, immune evasion, resistance and intervention mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Infer host-pathogen feedback and immune-evasion mechanisms from longitudinal and perturbation evidence.
Compare pathogen adhesion, invasion, toxin and persistence mechanisms and distinguish direct from immune-mediated damage.
Explain antimicrobial resistance and vaccine/prophylactic intervention mechanisms and evaluate selection and efficacy limitations.

practice: Analyze archived infection and resistance cases and compare mechanistic hypotheses without designing pathogen enhancement.

includes: ATP/redox accounting, glycolysis, respiration, photosynthetic energy conversion, biosynthesis and metabolic regulation.

outcomes.description: Explain major biosynthetic routes and integrate allosteric, hormonal and compartmental regulation across metabolic states.
Trace central catabolic and photosynthetic energy-conversion pathways and predict consequences of blocked steps.
Balance carbon, reducing equivalents and ATP and evaluate coupled-reaction free-energy direction.

practice: Solve isotope and energy-accounting cases and predict metabolite changes under defined nutritional and enzyme perturbations.

includes: Bacterial, archaeal and microbial-eukaryotic physiology; growth/media/asepsis; identification, biofilms and microbial ecology.

outcomes.description: Explain biofilm, symbiotic and biogeochemical functions and distinguish culture-based from community-sequence evidence.
Design approved aseptic cultivation and dilution-count measurements and calculate growth and viable counts.
Compare microbial cellular, metabolic and genetic strategies and use diagnostic traits to identify major groups.

practice: Characterize an approved teaching microorganism or archived culture dataset using growth, microscopy and identification evidence.

includes: DNA replication/repair/recombination, transcription, RNA processing, translation and prokaryotic/eukaryotic gene regulation.

outcomes.description: Explain DNA maintenance mechanisms and predict mutation and repair phenotypes from molecular lesions.
Trace gene expression through RNA processing and translation and predict sequence-to-product consequences.
Compare regulatory logic across organisms and infer transcriptional, chromatin and post-transcriptional control from perturbations.

practice: Interpret mutation, reporter and rescue experiments and construct falsifiable gene-regulatory explanations.

includes: Membrane voltage/conductance, action potentials, synapses, circuits, sensory/motor systems, plasticity and neural dysfunction.

outcomes.description: Use locally taught Nernst and conductance-current relations to interpret membrane and action-potential recordings.
Explain synaptic integration, excitation/inhibition and plasticity and infer circuit effects from perturbations.
Relate sensory, motor and learning-system organization to behavior and distinguish circuit dysfunction hypotheses.

practice: Analyze supplied voltage-clamp, spike and behavior records and compare alternative synaptic or circuit explanations.

includes: Bacteria, archaea, microbial eukaryotes, fungi, plants and animals; diagnostic traits, life cycles and body plans.

outcomes.description: Compare plant, fungal and animal body plans and relate structural organization to ecological constraints.
Compare reproductive and life-cycle strategies, including haploid/diploid transitions and symbiotic dependencies.
Identify major lineages using diagnostic traits and distinguish classification from superficial resemblance.

practice: Use identification keys and annotated specimens or images to build a comparative lineage and life-cycle portfolio.

includes: Sequence substitution, tree likelihood/pruning, topology search, support and phylogenetic comparative models.

outcomes.description: Fit locally derived phylogenetic covariance models and distinguish shared ancestry from independent trait association.
Construct continuous-time substitution models and calculate sequence-transition and tree-likelihood probabilities.
Implement likelihood pruning and bounded topology search and assess branch support and model misspecification.

practice: Implement a small phylogenetic likelihood calculation and compare tree and trait inferences under alternative models.

includes: Plant anatomy, water/mineral and sugar transport, photosynthetic physiology, hormones, development, reproduction and stress.

outcomes.description: Compare C3, C4 and CAM physiology and interpret photosynthetic and respiratory response curves.
Explain hormonal and environmental control of plant growth, flowering and reproductive development.
Predict drought, salinity, nutrient and biotic-stress responses and distinguish acclimation from adaptation.
Relate plant tissue structure to water potential, mineral acquisition and source-sink transport.

practice: Interpret plant transport and gas-exchange datasets and design an approved growth-response experiment.

includes: Selection/migration/mutation/drift recursions, linkage disequilibrium, coalescent models and quantitative-genetic response.

outcomes.description: Derive deterministic and finite-population allele-frequency models and analyze equilibrium, drift and linkage effects.
Derive elementary coalescent waiting-time and diversity predictions and evaluate demographic-identifiability limits.
Estimate additive genetic variance and derive multivariate response-to-selection predictions with environmental assumptions explicit.

practice: Derive population and coalescent predictions and analyze supplied genetic-variance and demographic datasets.

includes: Population/interactions dynamics, local stability, stage-structured demography, occupancy/count models and model selection.

outcomes.description: Construct stage-structured projection matrices and calculate growth, sensitivity and extinction-risk approximations.
Construct population and interaction ODEs and analyze equilibria and local Jacobian stability using derivatives taught locally.
Fit ecological count and occupancy models with explicit detection processes and evaluate predictive and mechanistic adequacy.

practice: Analyze demographic and repeated-survey data with matrix, ODE and detection-aware statistical models.

includes: Receptor signaling, pathway cross-talk, cell-fate control, apoptosis, tissue homeostasis and cancer evolution.

outcomes.description: Relate oncogenic alterations, genome instability and microenvironmental selection to tumor progression and resistance.
Explain cell-death, senescence and tissue-homeostasis mechanisms and distinguish their experimental signatures.
Infer receptor-to-effector pathway organization from dose, time and epistasis perturbation evidence.

practice: Interpret signaling and tumor-perturbation datasets and distinguish causal pathway effects from correlated markers.

includes: Diffraction/phasing, cryo-EM projection/reconstruction, NMR restraints, model refinement and structural validation.

outcomes.description: Use the projection-slice relation to explain cryo-EM alignment/reconstruction and diagnose heterogeneity and resolution artifacts.
Relate diffraction intensities, phases and electron density and explain crystallographic phasing and refinement workflows.
Translate assigned NMR proximity and coupling observations into structural restraints and evaluate underdetermination.
Evaluate molecular models against maps/restraints, geometry and held-out validation using taught molecular-viewer operations.

practice: Analyze supplied diffraction, cryo-EM and NMR-derived records and validate alternative structural models in a documented viewer workflow.

includes: Genetic circuit specification, approved assembly strategies, host burden, control, validation and containment.

outcomes.description: Plan approved nonpathogenic genetic assembly and verification using explicit sequence and assay constraints.
Design circuit validation, stability and containment tests and distinguish functional failure from measurement artifacts.
Specify genetic circuits and predict dynamic behavior, noise sensitivity and host-resource coupling.

practice: Develop and simulate a benign teaching circuit and prepare an institutionally reviewable construction and containment dossier.

includes: Biological network representations, mechanistic ODE models, flux-balance analysis, sensitivity and identifiability.

outcomes.description: Construct and implement biochemical ODE networks and analyze feedback, steady states and parameter sensitivity.
Build stoichiometric flux-balance models and interpret feasibility, objectives and alternative optima.
Estimate bounded model parameters and distinguish structural nonidentifiability, practical uncertainty and model discrepancy.

practice: Implement a gene/metabolic model, fit synthetic and archived observations and design measurements that distinguish competing mechanisms.

includes: Viral genome strategies, entry/replication/assembly, host range, viral evolution and infectivity/genome assays.

outcomes.description: Explain host range, persistence and viral evolutionary tradeoffs using receptor and population evidence.
Interpret plaque, endpoint-dilution and genome-copy measurements and distinguish infectivity from molecular detection.
Compare viral genome-to-replication strategies and predict host machinery and lifecycle dependencies.

practice: Analyze archived lifecycle and assay data and propose non-operational discriminating tests of replication hypotheses.

includes: Chemical safety, weighing, volumetric technique, titrimetry, gravimetry, blanks, standards and calibration uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Construct standard, blank and standard-addition calibrations and quantify detection limits and uncertainty.
Plan safe handling, storage, waste segregation and emergency responses from hazard information.
Perform or document validated volumetric and gravimetric analyses with stoichiometric endpoint calculations.

practice: Complete a supervised assay with blanks, replicate preparations, standards and a traceable uncertainty budget.

includes: Electronic configurations, periodic trends, Lewis/VSEPR, qualitative orbital bonding and intermolecular forces.

outcomes.description: Predict polarity, intermolecular interactions and qualitative bulk properties from molecular structure.
Construct Lewis, resonance, geometry and qualitative molecular-orbital representations and compare their limits.
Use electronic configurations and effective nuclear charge to explain periodic trends and exceptions.

practice: Construct competing molecular representations and justify geometry, bond-order and property predictions.

includes: Matter, elements, isotopes, ions, chemical formulas, stoichiometry, concentration and ideal gases.

outcomes.description: Relate atoms, isotopes, ions and formulas to mass, charge and composition.
Balance reactions and calculate limiting reagents, yields and mole-to-mass conversions.
Calculate concentration, dilution and ideal-gas quantities with unit and model checks.

practice: Solve composition and reaction-accounting problems and prepare a documented dilution plan.

includes: Electronic-structure calculations, geometry optimization, molecular dynamics, ensembles and free-energy sampling.

outcomes.description: Run and validate electronic-structure workflows with basis, convergence, geometry and method-sensitivity checks.
Estimate free-energy differences using locally derived perturbation and umbrella-reweighting formulas and assess overlap uncertainty.
Implement a simple force-field molecular-dynamics integrator and diagnose timestep, equilibration and ensemble errors.

practice: Reproduce a molecular energy difference and implement a small dynamics experiment with convergence and sampling audits.

includes: Coordination geometry/isomerism, crystal and ligand fields, magnetism, stability, substitution and redox mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Distinguish substitution and electron-transfer pathways and interpret kinetic and thermodynamic evidence.
Determine coordination geometries, isomers, electron counts and complex stability from ligand properties.
Construct ligand-field diagrams and predict spin, magnetism and qualitative electronic spectra.

practice: Determine unknown-complex structures and mechanisms from composition, magnetic, equilibrium and rate evidence.

includes: Nernst equilibria, electrochemical cells, interfacial charge, Butler-Volmer kinetics and diffusion-limited measurements.

outcomes.description: Use locally derived one-dimensional diffusion-flux and limiting-current models to interpret voltammetric measurements.
Derive electrode potentials and cell free energies with activity and reference-electrode conventions.
Interpret exchange currents, overpotentials and Butler-Volmer/Tafel behavior with mechanism limitations.

practice: Analyze polarization and voltammetry data, separating equilibrium, kinetic, resistance and transport contributions.

includes: Aquatic/soil/atmospheric speciation, partitioning, adsorption, transformation, compartment balances and environmental sampling.

outcomes.description: Construct compartment mass balances and predict partitioning, adsorption and transformation using taught isotherm and rate models.
Design environmental chemical sampling with preservation, blanks, recovery controls and detection-limit interpretation.
Calculate environmental acid-base, metal and redox speciation under stated equilibrium assumptions.

practice: Analyze a watershed or atmospheric-box case with chemical balances, uncertainty and a defensible sampling plan.

includes: Mass-action equilibria, reaction quotients, acid-base systems, precipitation, complexation and redox accounting.

outcomes.description: Calculate pH, buffer response and titration curves with approximation checks.
Solve elementary equilibrium mass balances and distinguish equilibrium constants from reaction quotients.
Balance redox reactions and track oxidation states and electron equivalents.
Calculate solubility and simple complexation equilibria, including competing-ion effects.

practice: Solve coupled speciation problems and compare exact algebraic balances with standard approximations.

includes: UV-visible and atomic analysis, chromatography, mass spectrometry, introductory IR and NMR interpretation.

outcomes.description: Calculate chromatographic retention, efficiency and resolution and choose defensible separation conditions.
Interpret ionization, mass-to-charge and isotope/fragment patterns and assess mass-spectral identification limits.
Select optical analytical methods and calculate calibrated concentrations while diagnosing matrix and spectral interference.
Use locally taught IR bands and NMR shift, integration and coupling rules to constrain small-molecule structures.

practice: Analyze a blinded mixture using supplied instrument records or supervised instruments and justify identification and quantification.

includes: Empirical rate laws, integrated kinetics, Arrhenius behavior, elementary mechanisms and steady-state approximations.

outcomes.description: Derive and apply integrated zero-, first- and second-order rate laws and half-life relations.
Derive rate predictions from elementary mechanisms using pre-equilibrium and steady-state assumptions.
Estimate reaction orders, rate constants and activation parameters from concentration-time and temperature data.

practice: Analyze supplied kinetic traces and discriminate mechanisms using derived rate laws and residual plots taught locally.

includes: s- and p-block structures, oxidation-state trends, electron-deficient/hypervalent bonding and representative transformations.

outcomes.description: Predict representative hydride, oxide, halide and organoelement transformations using bonding, acid-base and redox reasoning.
Explain main-group structural and oxidation-state trends, including inert-pair and electron-deficient behavior.

practice: Compare unfamiliar main-group compounds and construct balanced reaction networks with justified stability trends.

includes: Crystal lattices, stoichiometric/nonstoichiometric defects, powder diffraction and solid-state synthesis/property relations.

outcomes.description: Describe unit cells and defects and enforce composition and charge balance in nonstoichiometric solids.
Calculate Bragg spacings and index simple powder patterns while distinguishing phase and size effects.
Design solid-state or solution-based preparation routes and relate processing to phase, microstructure and properties.

practice: Identify phases from supplied diffraction patterns and propose a preparation route with defect and phase-control checks.

includes: Binding and structure-activity relationships, dose-response, exposure, metabolism, selectivity and lead optimization.

outcomes.description: Use locally taught clearance, partitioning and metabolic-liability models to evaluate exposure and selectivity tradeoffs.
Propose synthetically feasible lead modifications and design discriminating chemical and biological validation.
Analyze structure-activity and dose-response data while distinguishing potency, efficacy and assay artifacts.

practice: Prepare a lead-optimization proposal from supplied activity, exposure and synthesis data without clinical recommendations.

includes: Molecular rotation/vibration, selection rules, electronic transitions, line shapes and magnetic resonance dynamics.

outcomes.description: Derive electronic-transition intensities and interpret vibronic structure, broadening and relaxation.
Construct spin Hamiltonians and derive elementary NMR/EPR resonance, coupling and pulse-response behavior.
Derive rotational and vibrational level patterns and IR/Raman selection rules including symmetry constraints.

practice: Derive and assign model spectra and compare competing Hamiltonians against supplied frequency and intensity data.

includes: Electron-flow mechanisms for substitution/elimination, unsaturated additions, carbonyl, aromatic, radical and elementary pericyclic reactions.

outcomes.description: Construct alkene and alkyne addition mechanisms and predict regioselectivity and stereoselectivity.
Predict aromatic substitution pathways and directing effects using resonance and aromaticity arguments.
Construct carbonyl addition, acyl substitution and enolate mechanisms with acid-base consistency.
Distinguish radical-chain and elementary pericyclic pathways and predict products using taught orbital-phase rules.
Predict substitution and elimination pathways and stereochemical outcomes from substrate and conditions.

practice: Solve unseen mechanism and product problems, rejecting alternatives through charge, orbital and stereochemical checks.

includes: Functional groups, skeletal representations, conformations, stereochemistry, resonance, acidity and elementary electronic effects.

outcomes.description: Translate names, skeletal formulas and three-dimensional representations and identify functional groups.
Assign stereochemical relationships and configurations and compare conformational energies.
Use resonance, induction and acid-base equilibria to predict relative stability and reactive sites.

practice: Build molecular models and defend stereochemical, conformational and acidity rankings.

includes: Retrosynthesis, functional-group interconversion, protecting groups, stereocontrol, purification and structural verification.

outcomes.description: Plan purification and verify proposed products using combined spectra, yield and purity evidence.
Develop and compare multistep retrosynthetic routes using strategic disconnections and accessible precursors.
Choose chemoselective and stereoselective conditions and justify protecting-group and order-of-operation decisions.

practice: Prepare a justified synthesis dossier and execute an approved small-scale route or analyze archived reaction records.

includes: Metal-carbon bonding, electron counting, elementary organometallic steps and homogeneous catalytic mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Build and discriminate catalytic cycles using resting states, rate laws, labeling and deactivation evidence.
Construct oxidative-addition, reductive-elimination, insertion and elimination mechanisms with stereochemical predictions.
Analyze organometallic bonding, electron counts and ligand effects on reactive intermediates.

practice: Prepare a mechanism dossier comparing catalytic proposals against kinetics, isotope labels and selectivity.

includes: Transition-state theory, master/rate equations, network timescales, diffusion-controlled reaction models.

outcomes.description: Derive elementary diffusion-controlled encounter rates from steady radial flux and compare transport versus activation control.
Construct reaction-network equations and analyze steady states, timescale separation and kinetic identifiability.
Derive transition-state rate expressions from partition functions and evaluate their recrossing and tunneling limitations.

practice: Derive rate predictions and analyze competing reaction networks using partition-function and concentration-time evidence.

includes: Chemical potentials, partial molar quantities, activities/fugacities, solution models and phase equilibria.

outcomes.description: Derive chemical-potential and partial-molar relations and connect reaction Gibbs energy to equilibrium.
Calculate nonideal mixture properties using activities, fugacities and excess free-energy models.
Construct phase diagrams and solve coexistence conditions using chemical potentials and phase-rule constraints.

practice: Derive and calculate binary-mixture coexistence and compare ideal and nonideal predictions with phase data.

includes: Step/chain-growth polymerization, molecular-weight distributions, chain statistics and polymer solution/phase behavior.

outcomes.description: Calculate number/weight averages and dispersity and interpret size-exclusion and chain-statistical measurements.
Apply locally developed chain-entropy and Flory-Huggins models to predict polymer mixing and phase separation.
Compare step-growth, radical and controlled-chain polymerizations and calculate conversion-dependent chain lengths.

practice: Design a target polymer and analyze conversion, distribution and phase data against explicit synthesis models.

includes: Born-Oppenheimer separation, molecular Hamiltonians, variational orbitals, Hartree-Fock and electron-correlation foundations.

outcomes.description: Distinguish exchange, static and dynamic correlation and explain configuration-interaction and density-functional approximations.
Construct molecular Hamiltonians and justify Born-Oppenheimer and elementary orbital approximations.
Derive variational matrix equations and the self-consistent-field principle for approximate molecular orbitals.

practice: Derive small-basis molecular calculations by hand and compare approximate energies with supplied reference results.

includes: Radioisotope activity/counting, decay chains, chemical yield, radiochemical separation and isotope tracing.

outcomes.description: Interpret tracer dilution and labeling experiments while distinguishing isotope exchange and chemical transformation.
Design isotope separation and recovery controls using chemical selectivity and contamination accounting.
Calculate activity, efficiency-corrected counts and elementary parent-daughter decay with uncertainty.

practice: Analyze archived counting and recovery data and design a tracer study with explicit radiation-control requirements.

includes: Host-guest recognition, cooperativity, self-assembly landscapes and stimuli-responsive molecular systems.

outcomes.description: Derive binding polynomials and distinguish affinity, avidity and cooperativity using competition data.
Propose responsive assemblies and specify controls separating reversible switching from degradation or aggregation.
Design self-assembling structures and predict equilibrium, kinetic trapping and defect consequences.

practice: Develop a quantitative assembly proposal with binding equations, competing hypotheses and validation measurements.

includes: Heat, work, internal energy, enthalpy, calorimetry, Hess cycles, entropy and Gibbs energy at algebraic depth.

outcomes.description: Apply energy conservation to calorimetry and distinguish heat, work, temperature and state functions.
Interpret entropy and calculate Gibbs-energy changes and equilibrium relations under stated temperature assumptions.
Calculate reaction enthalpies using calorimetric data, formation values and Hess cycles.

practice: Analyze a calorimetry dataset and construct a complete thermochemical cycle with sign and uncertainty checks.

includes: Concentration and generalization bounds, positive-definite kernels, RKHS foundations, EM and variational inference.

outcomes.description: Construct positive-definite kernels, establish the representer principle and solve regularized kernel learning problems.
Derive EM and variational lower bounds and implement latent-variable inference with convergence diagnostics.
Derive representative concentration, uniform-convergence and capacity-dependent generalization bounds.

practice: Prove a learning bound and implement latent-variable and kernel methods on identifiable synthetic benchmarks.

includes: Correctness and recurrence analysis, divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic programming, graph and randomized algorithms.

outcomes.description: Prove algorithm correctness using invariants and induction and solve runtime recurrences.
Design divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic-programming solutions and justify their applicability.
Implement and prove shortest-path, spanning-tree and flow algorithms under stated graph assumptions.
Analyze elementary randomized algorithms using expectation and failure probabilities.

practice: Implement alternative algorithms, prove correctness and compare measured scaling with derived bounds.

includes: Heuristic/adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, first-order knowledge representation, planning and Bayesian networks.

outcomes.description: Implement heuristic and adversarial search and prove admissibility or pruning conditions.
Represent knowledge with clauses and constraints and implement unification, resolution and elementary planning.
Construct Bayesian networks and perform exact inference using conditional-independence factorization.

practice: Build a search-and-planning agent and compare symbolic and probabilistic reasoning on controlled incomplete-information tasks.

includes: Lexing/parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate representations, dataflow, optimization and code generation.

outcomes.description: Generate executable code with register allocation, calling conventions and differential correctness tests.
Build typed intermediate representations and perform dataflow-based, semantics-preserving optimizations.
Construct tokenizers, grammars and parsers and diagnose ambiguity and syntax errors.

practice: Implement an end-to-end compiler for a small language and compare execution against its reference interpreter.

includes: P/NP completeness, space complexity, hierarchy theorems, randomized classes and proof-system perspectives.

outcomes.description: Prove NP-completeness and related hardness results with polynomial reductions and certificates.
Compare randomized complexity classes and derive amplification and elementary interactive-proof guarantees.
Analyze space-bounded computation and prove representative hierarchy and simulation results.

practice: Write full hardness proofs and analyze resource bounds and error amplification for randomized procedures.

includes: Finite automata, regular/context-free languages, pushdown machines, Turing machines and undecidability.

outcomes.description: Construct automata and grammars and prove language closure and nonrecognizability results.
Specify Turing-machine computations and prove equivalence of elementary computability models.
Prove undecidability by diagonalization and mapping reductions and distinguish recognition from decision.

practice: Construct machines and complete reduction proofs with both directions and encoding assumptions explicit.

includes: Binary representation, Boolean circuits, sequential logic, instruction sets, datapaths, pipelines and caches.

outcomes.description: Construct Boolean and sequential circuits and calculate integer and floating-point encodings.
Trace assembly instructions through datapaths and analyze pipeline hazards.
Calculate cache and memory-access behavior and explain locality and hierarchy tradeoffs.

practice: Build a small processor in a taught logic simulator and trace assembly and cache-access sequences.

includes: Image formation and convolution, camera geometry, feature matching, multiview inference and visual recognition.

outcomes.description: Model image formation and implement spatial/frequency filtering while accounting for sampling and noise.
Estimate camera and multiview geometry using correspondences, least squares and robust consensus fitting taught locally.
Build recognition or segmentation systems and evaluate geometric, domain-shift and subgroup failure modes.

practice: Implement a calibrated two-view reconstruction and a recognition pipeline with held-out geometric and statistical tests.

includes: Security games, pseudorandomness, symmetric encryption/MACs, public-key encryption, signatures and key exchange.

outcomes.description: Analyze signature and key-exchange protocols, including composition, randomness and misuse failures.
Construct modular-arithmetic public-key schemes and relate security to stated computational assumptions.
Define symmetric security games and prove elementary encryption and authentication reductions.

practice: Implement toy constructions for testing and write reduction proofs; distinguish educational code from deployable cryptography.

includes: Arrays, linked structures, stacks/queues, hashing, trees, heaps, graphs and asymptotic operation costs.

outcomes.description: Calculate asymptotic time and space costs and distinguish worst-case, average and amortized arguments.
Represent graphs with matrices and adjacency structures and implement basic traversals.
Implement hash tables, search trees and heaps and explain collision and balancing tradeoffs.
Implement sequence, stack and queue abstractions while maintaining representation invariants.

practice: Implement interchangeable structures and benchmark workloads while checking invariants and operation counts.

includes: Relational algebra and SQL, dependencies and normalization, indexes, query plans, transactions and recovery.

outcomes.description: Compare index, join and query-plan costs and implement an elementary relational operator.
Design normalized schemas and express queries in relational algebra and SQL with null and multiplicity semantics.

includes: Many-body Green functions, response and quasiparticles; Berry phases and elementary topological band invariants.

outcomes.description: Derive many-body Green-function and linear-response relations and interpret quasiparticle and collective signatures.
Calculate Berry phases and elementary band invariants and connect them to protected response and boundary states.

practice: Reconstruct an established quantum-matter result from a model Hamiltonian and compare its predicted response with supplied data.

includes: Physical models, dimensions, operational measurement, instrument resolution and elementary uncertainty propagation.

outcomes.description: Read basic mechanical and electrical instruments and distinguish resolution, calibration and precision.
Propagate elementary sum/product uncertainties and distinguish random variation from systematic error.
Formulate measurable physical models and check dimensions, scaling and limiting cases.

practice: Measure a simple physical relationship, record instrument limitations and construct a dimensionally checked uncertainty report.

includes: Vector kinematics, Newton laws, force models, conservation laws, rotation, gravitation and elementary orbits.

outcomes.description: Apply work-energy and momentum conservation to collisions and variable-force problems.
Calculate gravitational fields, effective orbital energies and elementary circular/Keplerian relations.
Construct free-body diagrams and solve translational motion with constraints and friction.
Calculate torques, moments of inertia and angular momentum for rigid-body motion.

practice: Solve multirepresentation mechanics problems and test a conservation prediction with video or supervised apparatus.

includes: Nuclear binding and shell/collective models, decay, reactions, cross sections and detector observables.

outcomes.description: Interpret radiation-detector spectra, selection rules and nuclear-measurement backgrounds using taught response models.
Calculate nuclear decay and reaction energetics, barriers and elementary cross sections.
Compare liquid-drop, shell and collective nuclear models and calculate binding, spin and parity predictions.

practice: Analyze archived nuclear spectra and reaction data with conservation, selection-rule and detector-response checks.

includes: Ray optics, imaging, interference, diffraction, resolution and polarization.

outcomes.description: Calculate slit/grating interference and diffraction and quantify resolution limits.
Trace rays through mirrors and lenses and calculate imaging, magnification and elementary aberration effects.
Represent polarization states and calculate polarizer and waveplate transformations.

practice: Design an imaging or diffraction measurement and compare observed patterns with analytic predictions.

includes: Particle quantum numbers, symmetry/conservation, Standard Model interactions, decays and collision-event reconstruction.

outcomes.description: Calculate invariant masses and elementary decay/collision rates and interpret significance, acceptance and background effects.
Use particle quantum numbers and discrete/continuous symmetries to determine allowed interactions and decays.
Explain Standard Model matter, gauge interactions and symmetry breaking using explicitly taught representation notation.

practice: Reconstruct candidate particles from archived four-vectors and compare signal and background hypotheses.

includes: Gaussian beams and resonators, gain and laser rate equations, nonlinear polarization and phase matching.

outcomes.description: Derive laser rate equations and calculate threshold, gain saturation and relaxation behavior.
Derive elementary nonlinear-polarization mixing and phase-matching predictions under slowly varying envelope assumptions.
Calculate Gaussian-beam propagation and resonator stability using explicitly taught paraxial matrix methods.

practice: Design a resonator and nonlinear conversion experiment using analytic beam, gain and phase-matching calculations.

includes: Debye screening, kinetic distributions, Vlasov moments, magnetohydrodynamics, plasma waves and instabilities.

outcomes.description: Derive magnetohydrodynamic balances and analyze flux freezing, equilibrium and resistive breakdown.
Calculate plasma scales and derive elementary kinetic and moment descriptions with collisionality assumptions.
Derive representative plasma dispersion relations and diagnose damping and instability mechanisms.

practice: Derive wave and equilibrium models and interpret supplied laboratory or space-plasma spectra.

includes: Classical field actions, canonical/path-integral quantization, scalar/spinor fields, diagrams and perturbative renormalization.

outcomes.description: Construct relativistic field actions and quantize free scalar and spinor fields with correct statistics.
Derive propagators and elementary diagrammatic scattering amplitudes using perturbative field methods.
Regularize representative loop integrals and explain counterterms, scale dependence and effective-field-theory validity.

practice: Derive a field-theory scattering calculation through a representative loop correction with regulator and symmetry checks.

includes: Wavefunctions, operators, measurement, one-dimensional Schrodinger systems, oscillator algebra, spin and tensor-product states.

outcomes.description: Normalize states and calculate measurement probabilities, expectations, commutators and uncertainty relations.
Solve standard bound and scattering-barrier Schrodinger models and derive harmonic-oscillator spectra.
Calculate spin measurements and tensor-product states and distinguish entanglement from classical correlation.

practice: Solve quantum models analytically and compare wavefunction, matrix and measurement representations.

includes: Quantized optical modes, coherent/squeezed states, photon statistics, correlation detection and atom-light models.

outcomes.description: Calculate optical correlation functions and interpret photon-counting and homodyne measurements.
Derive two-level light-matter and dissipative cavity dynamics and identify classical versus quantum signatures.
Construct Fock, coherent and squeezed optical states and calculate field and photon-number observables.

practice: Calculate correlation and cavity-response predictions and analyze archived photon-counting or homodyne data.

includes: Photoelectric and interference evidence, photon/matter-wave relations, atomic levels and radioactive decay at algebraic depth.

outcomes.description: Calculate elementary spectral transitions and distinguish atomic-model predictions from their limitations.
Use photon and de Broglie relations to interpret experiments that defeat classical particle or wave accounts.
Distinguish decay types and calculate activity, half-life and attenuation using exponential models.

practice: Interpret archived photoelectric, spectral and decay data with algebraic models and explicit model comparisons.

includes: Lorentz transformations, spacetime intervals, simultaneity, four-momentum and relativistic collisions.

outcomes.description: Calculate Lorentz transformations, intervals and time-order relations using spacetime diagrams.
Use four-momentum conservation to solve relativistic collision, decay and threshold problems.

practice: Solve frame-dependent descriptions of the same event and verify invariant energy-momentum results.

includes: Microcanonical/canonical/grand ensembles, fluctuations, classical gases, quantum occupancy statistics and phase transitions.

outcomes.description: Analyze interacting spin models using mean-field and scaling arguments and identify their critical limitations.
Derive ensemble distributions and calculate partition functions, thermodynamic observables and fluctuations.
Derive Bose and Fermi occupancy distributions from explicitly introduced indistinguishability assumptions and apply ideal-gas limits.

practice: Derive ensemble predictions for gases and spin systems and compare finite-size and thermodynamic-limit behavior.

includes: Thermodynamic laws, reversible/irreversible processes, engines, potentials, Maxwell relations, response and stability.

outcomes.description: Use entropy and free-energy extrema to determine equilibrium, stability and phase-coexistence conditions.
Apply thermodynamic laws to reversible and irreversible processes and derive engine-efficiency limits.
Construct thermodynamic potentials and derive Maxwell and response-function relations.

practice: Analyze thermodynamic cycles and derive response identities and stability inequalities from explicit potentials.

includes: Free, damped and driven oscillators, coupled modes, traveling/standing waves, interference and wave-energy transport.

outcomes.description: Calculate interference, beats and wave intensity and relate energy transport to oscillation amplitude.
Derive oscillator amplitude, phase and resonance and calculate coupled normal modes.
Construct traveling and standing-wave solutions and apply boundary, phase and group-speed relations.

practice: Analyze resonance and standing-wave measurements and compare amplitude/phase data with analytic models.
